what_worked: Following prior reflection: prioritizing deduplication and handler maps over Extract Method — these patterns actually reduce aggregate CC (17 point reduction vs 0 for prior audit's extract method patterns)
Shared utility extraction (Pattern 1) was the simplest refactor — just export existing functions and import them. Zero risk, immediate CC reduction

Handler map pattern (Patterns 2-3) was mechanical and reliable — define a map constant, replace if-chain with lookup + single guard. Required `as unknown as` cast for TS narrowing limitation but functionally safe
Concentrating all 3 patterns on one file (transcript.ts) was efficient — each pattern built on the previous, and the file's test coverage validated all changes
surprises: TypeScript cannot narrow discriminated union types through map lookups — `Record<string, V>` always returns `V` (not `V | undefined`) unless `noUncheckedIndexedAccess` is enabled. This required using `{ [key: string]: V | undefined }` instead, and `as unknown as` casts after the map check

The `isGroupedFileReadSegment` type predicate (`segment is ToolTranscriptSegment`) conflicts with prior narrowing — if TS already knows segment is ToolTranscriptSegment, negating the predicate produces `never`. This is a TS design limitation when combining type guards with discriminated union narrowing

Handler maps don't reduce CC as much as expected in the metric — replacing 6 if-blocks with 1 map lookup + 1 guard only reduces CC by ~5 per map because the map itself adds a branch. The real win is in cognitive complexity (readability) and maintainability (adding a new kind is one line)
next_time: When applying handler map patterns to discriminated unions in TS, type the map as `{ [key: string]: V | undefined }` and expect to use `as unknown as` casts for downstream type narrowing. This is safe because the map guarantees only valid variants reach the cast
